etymologies.etymologyHTML: From save +‎ -ing.

definitions.definition: A reduction in cost or expenditure.
(countable, usually in the plural) Something (usually money) that is saved, particularly money that has been set aside for the future.
(uncountable) The action of the verb to save.

quote.citation: 1692, Roger L’Estrange, “ (please specify the fable number.) (please specify the name of the fable.)”, in Fables, of Æsop and Other Eminent Mythologists: […], London:  […]  R[ichard] Sare, […], →OCLC:
quote.text: Tis Good Advice not to Contend with Those that are too Strong for us, but still with a saving to Honesty and Justice

definitions.definition: present participle and gerund of save
(theology) That saves someone from damnation; redemptive. [from 14th c.]

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Psalms 28:8:
quote.text: He is the saving strength of his anointed.

quote.citation: 1932, Lewis Grassic Gibbon, Sunset Song (A Scots Quair), Polygon, published 2006, page 14:
quote.text: Three of her bairns were drowned at sea, fishing off the Bervie braes they had been, but the fourth, the boy Cospatric, him that died the same day as the Old Queen, he was douce and saving and sensible, and set putting the estate to rights.

definitions.definition: Bringing back in returns or in receipts the sum expended; incurring no loss, though not gainful.
(in compound adjectives) Relating to making a saving.
With the exception of; except; save.

quote.text: And in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.
